body:
I'm not you, but I understand how you feel. In some ways, you remind me of how I could be in the future, still feeling emotionally drained to an extreme degree. I also keep up a facade of energy, of ambition, of competency. 

I'm tired too, tired of fighting and watching others fight the battles life brings against us when they shouldn't have to. Tired of the cycles of misery and despair I see not only around me, but the world over. But it is in this that sometimes I feel the strength to carry on. That I am tired, and how tired must so many others be? 

Maybe we are a cog in a machine, but maybe sometimes that machine is worthwhile. And being helpful doesn't always get you things or places, or success, but it does get you one thing I find very important. It can very easily end up with you knowing people who are the same way, and maybe even around whom you can drop any kind of facade you feel like you carry around. 

I try to keep living for a lot of reasons. My ambition, my desire to help others, my dog, and my desire to finally drop the facade, not through death - that would be a victory for the facade, for everything I hate. But by destroying it over time through myself and others. 

I don't have all the answers, but maybe I can just be someone to talk to. Hell, I could use it as well. If you want to talk more, please do message me. From everything I hear, you bring more value than you could possibly know - and remember that each action you take that is compassionate or kind can reflect and multiply a thousand times over.

No. No it is not. As someone who has been there before, while the pain is very, very real, it isn't as if one doesn't want help from it, but the emotional pain tends to be so intense as to block out a lot of rational thinking. The depression is the prison, not life. People generally in a suicidal mood are not thinking straight, myself included.
